title: What is Debugging?
description: Debugging is the systematic process of identifying, analyzing, and resolving bugs or defects in software to ensure it functions as intended.
solution:
1. Isolate the faulty code.
2. Reproduce the bug.
3. Analyze state using logs or debuggers.
4. Fix and verify.
tip: Always tackle one bug at a time to avoid complex side effects.

title: Undefined is not a function
description: This occurs when you attempt to call a value as a function, but that value is undefined. Usually due to missing imports or scope issues.
solution: Check if the function exists before calling it or ensure it's properly assigned.
tip: Use optional chaining: obj.calculate?.() to prevent crashes.

title: 404 Not Found vs 500 Server Error
description: 404 means the endpoint doesn't exist (client error). 500 means the server crashed while processing the request (backend error).
solution: For 404: Check URL spelling. For 500: Check backend logs and database connectivity.
tip: Always implement global error boundaries in your API services.

title: The Overflow Nightmare
description: Content leaking out of its container usually happens when fixed widths are used or flexbox properties aren't constrained.
solution: Use overflow: hidden or max-width: 100% to contain child elements.
tip: Use 'overflow-x: hidden' on the body tag as a safety net for mobile layouts.

title: The Missing 'await' Trap
description: Forgetting 'await' before a promise returns the Promise object instead of the resolved data, leading to unexpected 'Promise <pending>' values.
solution: Always use await: const data = await fetchUser();
tip: Use try/catch blocks with async functions to handle rejected promises gracefully.

title: Unit Testing 101
description: Unit tests focus on testing individual components or functions in isolation from the rest of the app.
solution: Write tests that cover edge cases, not just the happy path.
tip: Good tests should be independent, fast, and repeatable.

title: Chrome DevTools: Network Tab
description: The Network tab is your eyes into the communication between your app and the server.
example: // Filter by 'Fetch/XHR' to see API calls
solution: Inspect headers, payloads, and response status codes to find API bottlenecks.
tip: Use 'Throttling' to simulate slow 3G connections and test loading states.

title: Rubber Duck Debugging
description: Explain your problem out loud to an inanimate object. Translating the problem into words often exposes the logical flaw in your approach.
solution:
1. Step away from typing.
2. Explain the code line-by-line.
3. Notice the incorrect assumptions.
tip: Writing the problem down in a notebook has a similar cognitive effect.

title: Isolate the Bug
description: Remove layers of complexity. Create a minimal reproducible example (MRE). If the bug disappears, the issue is in the removed code.
solution:
1. Comment out unrelated code.
2. Hardcode variables to bypass external factors.
3. Test the broken logic in isolation.
tip: Codepen or CodeSandbox are great for building minimal reproducible examples.

title: Use Version Control (Git Bisect)
description: If a bug suddenly appears, use git bisect to find the exact commit that introduced the problem by performing a binary search on the history.
example:
$ git bisect start
$ git bisect bad HEAD
$ git bisect good v1.2.0
# Git checks out a midpoint for you to test.
solution:
1. Find a known good state.
2. Narrow down the offending commit.
3. Review the diff to understand what broke.
tip: Keep commits small and focused so identifying the root cause is easier.

title: 1xx & 2xx: Informational & Success
description: The 'Communication' and 'Happy Path' codes. 1xx means 'Wait, I'm thinking', while 2xx means 'I've done exactly what you asked'.
solution: Ensure your UI provides positive feedback (success toasts) when receiving 2xx status codes.
tip: Use 204 for DELETE or UPDATE operations where returning data is unnecessary.

title: 3xx: The Redirection Protocol
description: The user is being asked to take additional action to fulfill the request. Often used for URL restructuring or cached content.
solution: Double-check redirect loops and ensure 304 is handled by your browser cache to save bandwidth.
tip: Always use 301 for SEO when migrating pages to new URLs.

title: 4xx: Client Interaction Errors
description: These errors mean 'The request contains bad syntax or cannot be fulfilled.' This is almost always a problem on the frontend or a bad URL.
solution: Log the request payload and headers. Ensure the user is authenticated and the URL is spelled correctly.
tip: 403 means the server knows who you are but still says 'No'. 401 means the server doesn't know you.

title: 5xx: Server Infrastructure Failures
description: The server failed to fulfill an apparently valid request. This is a backend or infrastructure level problem.
solution: Check backend logs, cloud environment health, and database connection strings.
tip: A 504 error usually means a backend function timed out or a heavy database query failed.
